purpose: Owner-review draft: the click-through scene script for the shared tier-5 event (The Cold Roost, accepted M1 pilot). The chapter opens when any egg family reaches tier 5; the shared opening establishes the frost and the three threatened clutches; the player chooses one currently unlocked egg inside the scene; the choice selects the route telling; Neet is dispatched; after the two-minute trip the player opens a click-through continuation that adapts the selected Cold Roost telling and Neet's distinct viewpoint - the player sees what happened through the trip, not only its result. One pilot only (Neet, tier 5, Tend the Nesting Grounds, all three egg routes). It is one shared event with a common spine and three different lasting outcomes, not three separate adventures. Tier-5 pack entries are viewpoint texts (kind 'viewpoint', no hook/outcome pair), so - a documented deviation from tiers 1-4 - there are no byte-quote boxes here: confirm and final beats are labeled adaptations, and the mapping layer carries per-beat provenance. Nothing here edits data/, source/, or the playable HTML.

Presentation feel reference: the game's existing click-through arrival scene (Tia) - short boxes, click to advance
presentationModel: Player opens the tier-5 chapter when any egg family reaches the tier. The shared opening establishes the frost and the three threatened clutches; inside the scene the player chooses one currently unlocked egg, and that choice selects the route telling. Neet is dispatched; when the trip finishes, the player opens a click-through continuation that adapts the selected telling and Neet's viewpoint into paced beats: the crisis, the keepers' work on the crag, the hatching, the protected crag and almanac records, and the route's lasting consequence. Other unlocked eggs remain available on later trips - one shared event, three tellings, no canon lock. Per the accepted premise and HANDOFF.md, the completed scene is stored for rereading in the replay journal and does not replay automatically on later visits.
playerFlow: op-01 -> op-02 -> op-03 -> op-04 -> choice (one to three unlocked eggs) -> confirm = adapted plight box for the chosen family (no byte-quote pair exists at tier 5) -> one route departure box (intent only) -> trip-start (dispatch, no result) -> trip timer -> trip-end (click to open the report) -> route return beats in order, last box = adapted route outcome. Hatching, the protected crag, the almanac record, and route-specific consequences all arrive after the trip. After the chapter, other unlocked eggs remain available on later trips.

implementationNotes.chapterOpen: The chapter becomes available as soon as any egg material family reaches tier 5. Suggested UI copy, outside the story beats: 'New chapter - Tend the Nesting Grounds, tier 5.'
implementationNotes.optionGating: Show only options for egg families currently unlocked at this tier; one, two, or three options are all valid states. The opening prose is written to hold when only one option exists, and each telling covers what the week did for all three clutches.
implementationNotes.routeLock: The egg choice sets the active route for this trip; other unlocked choices remain available on later trips, one active route at a time. No route is canon-locked: later chapters may assume only the spine facts (S1-S7) and choice-independent growth, never that a particular telling was seen.
implementationNotes.replayJournal: Per shared-events.json premise and HANDOFF.md, the completed scene is stored for rereading in the replay journal and does not replay automatically on later visits.
implementationNotes.tripTimer: The trip runs about two minutes on the game timer. The timer belongs to implementation and UI, not to story text.
implementationNotes.awardHandling: The script never states or implies that the player receives the chosen egg: the egg names which situation the telling focuses, not freight. source/core.js:269 awards stamps, likeability, boosts, and bonuses only - no ingredient, no egg - and the M1 pilot's section 0.5 owner question frames the selected material as story focus. The trip-end beat only opens Neet's report; awarding belongs to the game's existing systems, outside story text.

beatRules: Every beat carries id, phase, speaker, portrait, text. The choice beat additionally carries its note and option moments.

Narrator beats stay brief and set place, action, or a visible action. The route tellings are prose, so the tellings' work is carried in narrator beats with reported speech where the accepted sources narrate a line (the introduction and catch labels, the piton report); Neet's viewpoint layer becomes her own voiced beats at the points her private record forms. No new dialogue is invented for Claire, Dolbur, or Kyle; Daisy speaks only her documented floor line, which has its own speaker beat.
Each box is written to be comfortable in a dialogue box: about 40 words per box, hard target 43 audit tokens.

No byte-quote boxes at tier 5 (documented deviation from tiers 1-4): the pack's tier-5 entries have no hook/outcome pair. The confirm adapts the chosen family's standing plight, the final box adapts the route's lasting outcome, and the mapping section cites each beat's source parts.
Adaptation rule: no long event paragraph goes into a single box; every beat re-paces accepted content without changing its facts; the three route tellings keep their own facts and sequence.

Speaker 'narrator' is unvoiced scene text with no portrait. Speaker 'neet' shows the Neet portrait ('neet', verified in source/core.js TRAVELERS: Neet_Portrait.png). Claire, Daisy, Dolbur, and Kyle are established travelers with existing portrait assets (source/core.js TRAVELERS: ClairePortrait.png, DaisyPortrait.png, DolburPortrait.png, KylePortrait.png; files in assets/characters/). Daisy's one direct spoken line, life-r6, carries her portrait id 'daisy'. Claire, Dolbur, and Kyle have no spoken beats - their work is narrator-carried with portrait 'none', so their ids are recorded in the character notes rather than on beats. Engine note: the current beat renderer (source/app.js:177) shows a beat portrait only when a beat's portrait id equals the viewpoint traveler's own id - so 'daisy' is correct as data now, and displays if the renderer is extended to show co-star portraits.
No resolution appears anywhere before the trip ends. Pre-dispatch boxes carry spine-level facts (S1), the chosen family's standing plight, and Neet's spoken intentions only.

Shared-event discipline: route-owned lasting outcomes (Life: the mixed roost and its trellis feathers; Mana: the hush custom and the working rite; Stamina: the quarry household) appear only in their own routes after the trip and never cross routes; the spine facts S1-S7 are common ground. Within one route the cast acts only per the selected telling's roles.
Route independence: no beat assumes another family's route or an earlier Neet chapter was seen; no tier-1..4 callbacks; Neet's habits (ledger, margin, dry record voice) are shown fresh in each route.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The frost came early and did not send word ahead. By the first hard night, three wild clutches - bright as a rumor, singing in the dark, far too large for anyone's comfort - had come down from the high nests.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: They came down onto the one crag by the orchard, on a shelf of stone already leaning toward winter. Nobody owns wild things - that is the law of the region, and also the excuse of anyone who owes a favor.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: By the hour before dawn, five keepers held the same freezing watch - a shrine keeper, a warrior, a knight, a baker, a challenger - giant opinions, empty hands. The ledge would not wait, and neither, in the end, did anyone.

beats.speaker: neet
beats.text: So the ledger opens on a cold page, and the writing is mine to keep - three clutches, one frost, no owner anywhere in it. Tell me which egg I am minding until daylight, and I will write the night honestly.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Choose the egg Neet's night will follow.
beats.note: Only options whose egg family is unlocked at this tier are shown; one, two, or three options are all valid states. This is one shared event, The Cold Roost: the opening lines are true whichever egg is chosen, and each chosen telling covers what the week did for all three clutches. No route is canon-locked; the other eggs stay available on later trips. The chosen egg is the story's focus, never a settlement award.

options.teaser: Bright as a rumor, and loosest of the three on a shelf the frost is already testing.
Singing to itself in the dark - the smallest voice on the crag tonight.
Far too large for anyone's comfort, and the ledge under it is losing its grip on winter.

sharedDispatch.speaker: narrator
sharedDispatch.text: Neet takes the assignment and goes; whatever happens out there comes home with her.

sharedDispatch.speaker: narrator
sharedDispatch.text: The trip is over. Open Neet's report to see what happened, and how it ended.

confirmBeats.speaker: narrator
confirmBeats.text: The rainbow clutch's crisis was never cold alone - it was custody. Wild things do not accept strange eggs on the strength of a speech about community.

departureBeats.speaker: neet
departureBeats.text: Custody first, then. Warmth will have its own hands on this crag; the introductions are mine to make. You cannot hurry a crag into liking somebody - you can only arrange the meeting, and I intend to pay the mornings it asks for.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The report starts at the crag. The frost knocked the rainbow clutch free of its high nest before anyone had noticed it sat light there; by morning, the strange eggs lay cooling among ordinary ones, bright as sugar.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: She walked the ledges with her ledger and counted the neighbors. Every nest up there belonged to somebody, and no argument she could write would move an egg.

returnBeats.speaker: neet
returnBeats.text: The introductions will be made, not argued: a feather from the rainbow nest carried nose to nose, morning by morning, until the crag's birds read strangers as tenants. Nobody consents to a speech; everybody consents to a smell they know.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Daisy took the cold half of the problem: the ledge bricked in oven-warmed straw, heat only, tested against her cheek like checking proof, and every strange egg turned a quarter-twist twice a day, the way she steadies dough through its rise.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The first straw blanket went out too thick and insulated worse, and Daisy's answer to it became a sentence the ledger keeps in full.

returnBeats.speaker: daisy
returnBeats.text: That is all right. We can try again another time.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The first evening's work was testing how much weight the crag's stone would hold: Dolbur hauled himself up a rope and dropped the coil back down, and Kyle caught it one-handed.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: An introduction, Dolbur called it; a catch, said Kyle, more precisely - and they have opened with it ever since.

returnBeats.speaker: neet
returnBeats.text: The high nest has been empty long enough; the mother is not coming back. I wrote it in my margin, not aloud, and kept one rainbow feather for the fledging day.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: By the third morning, the crag had stopped noticing which eggs were strange: the introductions held, nose to feathered nose, and the ledges rode warm.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The rainbow chicks hatched into borrowed warmth, the bluebird and wyvern eggs hatched without incident the same week, and every egg of the frost came out of its shell safe.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: When the fledging came, the rainbow chicks spread over the whole roost - among bluebirds and along the wyvern family's edges - until the roost considered itself mixed, and did not stop to think when it had started.

returnBeats.speaker: neet
returnBeats.text: The roost's hatch-day goes into the shrine almanac tonight, in my own hand - the same hand as the margin note and the kept feather - and red, blue, and gold tellings begin their three-version record beside it.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Before the company scattered, Claire named the crag and reclassified it protected - the patrol schedule went up on the spot, in her handwriting, which is how the site held onto everything that happened there.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The frost, by Claire's log, broke inside the week and left the orchard untouched - trellis, fence, and fruit without a lasting scar.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: And the roost's lasting answer to the frost is beauty: every spring the fledglings' rainbow feathers turn up catching light along the orchard trellis, and the town walks out to see them - a mixed roost made famous, mostly, by its colors.

confirmBeats.speaker: narrator
confirmBeats.text: The bluebird clutch dulled overnight - shells gone from paint-bright to wet chalk, the song inside failing. Not an enemy, not a tangle, not a wind: a song losing its note.

departureBeats.speaker: neet
departureBeats.text: A song losing its note is no puzzle for paper. I will begin with the correct lullabies, as the rite teaches - and if the nest refuses the neatness, I will try the note it asks for instead.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The report starts at the crag before dawn: the bluebird clutch dulled overnight, the other two merely cooling, and on the far ledge a wyvern egg working loose - one event, three needs.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Every need had its keeper inside the week. Dolbur offered loudly to fight the frost; he was politely assigned elsewhere.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Neet led with the shrine's lullabies, every line of them correct - and the nest flatly refused each one; the chick sat through three correct verses and went duller with each.

returnBeats.speaker: neet
returnBeats.text: So the rite would be a heresy, and the first one I ever intend to keep. Not flat as a mistake - flat where the song rises, on purpose, until the note inside matches me instead of me matching it.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The wrong note needed practice. At midnight, in the shrine pantry, where her voice carries least, she worked the flat note until it sat where she wanted it.

returnBeats.speaker: neet
returnBeats.text: For the record: my midnight voice carries a little further than the pantry believes. The bakery was kind about it, and I am polite about not knowing they heard.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Then the rite ran, wrong by design: flat where the song rises, until the note inside matched her error and held it. Within two nights the shells brightened out of their wet chalk.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The rest was quiet logistics. Kyle wound cloth around the ladder's metal rungs so nothing would ring, and then held a still vigil for hours at a stretch while the rite ran.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: She counted the only way her ear can - by what interrupted: over the two nights of wrong verses, nothing rose from the wrapped rungs to answer, and the hush around her note did not shift once.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Daisy restocked the leaning ledges with oven-warmed straw, heat only, so the other two clutches rode warm; the bakers' quarter stayed muffled, and warm bread came down so nobody had to shout a meal.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Claire kept three nights of silence and wrote the rule the moment asked for: no voices past the tree line.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: On the coldest night, Kyle's ladder-foot slid on the icy rock; Dolbur, out on the high path taking the frost-line reading, dropped his spare rope down, and Kyle caught it mid-slip. Both called it an introduction; neither called it a rescue.

returnBeats.speaker: neet
returnBeats.text: The almanac gets the hatch-day. The rite record gets the method, exactly as run. What neither record gets is the margin note: some things mend when you stop correcting them.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: By the week's end every egg of the frost had hatched safe, and the roost's hatch-days went into the shrine almanac - red, blue, and gold - in the same tidy hand.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The frost broke inside the week and left the orchard without lasting damage. When the quiet held, the crag - named, protected - went onto the patrol schedule in Claire's hand: the site that asked for hush would get a watch.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The chick hatched healthy and sang flat all spring - the crag's mornings led by one patient bluebird - and its true song came back only after winter, the season the region remembers as quiet.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: What stayed was this: the wrong-lullaby rite on the shrine's records as a working rite, and a town that walks the orchard path hushed at nesting time, every spring.

confirmBeats.speaker: narrator
confirmBeats.text: The wyvern egg has rolled loose along the failing ledge's lip, and the other two clutches shiver through the frost. The mother came down circling - wide, patient, in no mood for committee.

departureBeats.speaker: neet
departureBeats.text: No climb moves one stone without her leave. I will have the compresses ready, a settling word learned by midnight, and her own signs read before anything shifts.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The report starts at the crag, with a rule of the place: nothing up there moves without the mother's leave, and the night's first work is learning what her leave looks like.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The mother's circling invited no advice: Claire's cordons closed the orchard path and every roofline a spectator might use, and the region's people, to their credit, stayed behind them.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Dolbur climbed the winter-hardened rock, and one piton bent on the first reach. He reported it before his boots were down, immediately and cheerfully - which is half of why the climb worked.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: He had started early because he had heard her first - a sound like stone getting annoyed, he said - so the climb was half-rigged while everyone else was still deciding who would climb.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Kyle anchored from the storeroom's spare rope and counted every carry. Neet's part was quieter: compresses and a settling word readied long before they were needed, and her eyes on the mother's wings and tail for the right hour.

returnBeats.speaker: neet
returnBeats.text: The lesson I learned and kept to myself: approach when her wings folded, wait when her tail set. One wrong guess and the committee convenes itself - and the ledger can suffer a blank when patience is the entry.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The hour was not ours to decide. Daisy had been up all night regardless, and what she carried out at first light settled the argument better than words could: a loaf, set down on the warm stone at the quarry's foot.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The mother circled once more over the stone, landed beside the loaf, and the landing decided it: the move went ahead under her leave.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Four carries later - dry stone, no blasting in its history, room to turn around - the brood was whole at the old quarry ledge, and the mother's next circle was drawn around them.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The carry baskets were lined with oven-warmed straw, heat only - the roost trick, by week's end, had earned its second career as courier-bedding.

returnBeats.speaker: neet
returnBeats.text: My margin, kept for myself: she was never guarding the old ledge. She was deciding whether the quarry was good enough - and the quarry was. Four carries say so better than I did.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: When the gear came down, the last coil dropped from the ledge straight into Kyle's waiting hands.

returnBeats.speaker: neet
returnBeats.text: The landing finished the argument, so I sent the only sign-off I had: one nod, from the correct distance, at a wyvern's eye level. It is not in any record, hers or ours.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The roost's hatch-days went into the shrine almanac as they came, one line beside the red and blue entries, in the same tidy hand as the rest of the frost week's bookkeeping.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: When Claire's cordons came down, they came down into something: the crag - named, protected - went onto the patrol schedule in her handwriting, and the quarry ledge went onto the map.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The frost broke inside seven days and left the orchard untouched. The moved egg hatched safe at the quarry - the first brood its new household ever raised - and the other two clutches hatched untroubled on the crag.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The crag lost a tenant and gained a neighbor: the wyvern household lives at the quarry ledge now, a fixed point on the map, on an adjusted patrol route - and the one the mother tolerates is Dolbur.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: And the first sentence of every version of that week stays the same, in the almanac and everywhere it is copied: nobody owns wild things.

mapping.legend: Tokens used in the per-beat citations below. [S1-spine] = shared-events.json shared opening text (the scene's common spine). [S2-spine]..[S7-spine] = the M1 pilot's spine fact rows (pilot-M1-cold-roost.md, fact table 0.1). [LT]/[MT]/[ST] = the Life/Mana/Stamina route tellings in shared-events.json. [VP-Life]/[VP-Mana]/[VP-Stamina] = Neet's tier-5 viewpoint texts (stories-v2/neet-t1-5.json; byte-identical to data/expedition-stories.json rows 0/1/2). [MD-1]..[MD-4.2] = pilot-M1-cold-roost.md sections (1 shared opening; 2 Life telling with 2.1 Daisy and 2.2 Claire perspectives; 3 Mana telling with 3.1 Neet and 3.2 Kyle perspectives; 4 Stamina telling with 4.1 Dolbur and 4.2 Daisy perspectives). [MAT]/[JOB] = data/game-data.json material names and data/expedition-jobs.json job name. Bracketed citations name accepted material; anything not covered by a token is scene glue and is listed as new fan-written in factProvenance and in mapping.notes.
mapping.sharedOpening: op-01..op-03 adapt the shared opening [S1-spine] almost sentence for sentence: the frost arriving without word; the three clutches and their three descriptors (bright as a rumor; singing in the dark; far too large for anyone's comfort); the one crag by the orchard and the shelf already leaning toward winter; the law and its excuse clause; the five-keeper roll-call with giant opinions and empty hands; and the ledge line. op-04 and the choice text are Neet's spoken glue in her ledger voice. The three option teasers are built from the S1 descriptors only (bright as a rumor; singing in the dark; far too large), so no telling-level detail precedes the choice. trip-start and trip-end reuse the series-standard dispatch lines of the tier-4 benchmark.

life.hook: life-hook adapts the Life telling's custody sentence ([LT]/[MD-2]: the crisis was not cold alone - it was custody) as the confirm plight. No byte-quote exists at tier 5: the pack carries a viewpoint text, not a hook.
life.scene: life-r1 sets the physical crisis from [LT] (knocked free of its high nest before anyone noticed it sat light there; cooling among ordinary ones, bright as sugar). life-r2 turns custody into her survey: every nest belongs to somebody ([LT]/[MD-2]), with the ledger-count imagery as glue. life-r3 brings [VP-Life]'s introductions (a feather carried nose to nose, morning by morning, until the crag reads strangers as tenants) as her spoken plan; the nobody-consents line is glue. life-r4 carries [LT]'s straw work (oven-warmed straw, heat only, quarter-twist twice a day like dough through its rise) plus [MD-2.1]'s cheek-test; life-r5/life-r6 carry [MD-2.1]'s thick-blanket failure and Daisy's documented floor line, quoted byte-exact as the only direct spoken line. life-r7/life-r8 carry the first-evening rope drop and catch ([LT]/[MD-2]/[S5-spine]) with both labels - an introduction, a catch - and the ever-since. life-r9 is [VP-Life]: the empty high nest, the mother not coming back, the margin written not aloud, one rainbow feather kept for the fledging day. life-r10 is [MD-2]'s third-morning line (the crag stopped noticing which eggs were strange) with glue. life-r11 carries [LT]/[S2-spine] (hatched into borrowed warmth; the other two without incident; every egg of the frost safe). life-r12 carries [LT]/[MD-2] fledge and the mixed roost (tail glue new). life-r13 carries the almanac record ([LT]/[S6-spine]) and [VP-Life]'s same-hand link between margin note, kept feather, and hatch-day line, with the three-version record. life-r14 carries the naming and protection ([LT]/[S3-spine]/[MD-2]: schedule in her handwriting on the spot; site holding on). life-r15 carries [S7-spine]/[LT]/[MD-2] (frost broke inside the week by Claire's log; trellis, fence, fruit).
life.outcome: life-out adapts the Life telling's lasting outcome ([LT]/[MD-2]): rainbow feathers catching light along the orchard trellis each spring, the town walking out, the roost famous mostly for beauty; the mixed-roost state is the route's consequence.
life.notes: Excluded on purpose: Claire's private perspective adds ([MD-2.2]) and Daisy's warm-center observation ([MD-2.1] adds) belong to their own future chapters and are not borrowed; Daisy's floor line enters only because the tellings' work keeps it visible. The wording 'the ledger keeps in full' (life-r5) is glue for MD's 'and she meant it'. 'Did not stop to think when it had started' (life-r12) and 'nose to feathered nose' (life-r10) are new texture lines. The choice teaser for this family is built from [S1-spine] descriptors only ('bright as a rumor'), so no telling detail leaks before the choice.

mana.hook: mana-hook adapts the Mana telling's crisis ([MT]/[MD-3]: dulled overnight, shells from paint-bright to wet chalk, the song inside failing; not an enemy, not a tangle, not a wind).
mana.scene: mana-r1 is the needs-map ([MT]/[MD-3]: one event, three needs). mana-r2 stages [MD-3]'s joke fact: Dolbur offered loudly to fight the frost; politely assigned elsewhere. mana-r3 carries [MT]/[VP-Mana] correct lullabies refused and [MD-3.1]'s three correct verses dulled further. mana-r4 stages the decision ([MT] sang wrong on purpose; [VP-Mana] the difficult part was learning to sing badly) as her spoken line; the heresy framing is glue. mana-r5 carries [VP-Mana]/[MD-3.1] midnight pantry practice where her voice carries least. mana-r6 stages [MD-3.1]'s bakery-awake joke in her voice (glue: 'the pantry believes'). mana-r7 carries [MT] the match and hold plus shells brightened within two nights. mana-r8 carries [MT] Kyle's cloth-wrapped rungs, their sound-damping purpose, and the hours-long still vigil; the [MD-3.2] perspective aside 'he had heard them ring half the climb up' was removed on the owner's second revision pass, so the beat keeps only the telling's visible work. mana-r9 is a connective beat written from Neet's own register (owner revision pass): she counts only what her ear can measure of the shared work - the interruptions of her rite against the wrapped rungs and the steady hush around her note; it deliberately carries none of [MD-3.2]'s reserved private material (the count of seventeen silences, the pride in the hush holding without him). mana-r10 carries [MT] straw restocks for the other ledges plus [MD-3.2]/[MD-0.3] muffled quarter and warm bread so nobody shouts. mana-r11 carries [MD-3]/[MD-0.3] Claire's three nights of silence and the no-voices rule. mana-r12 carries [MT]/[MD-3.2]/[S5-spine] the coldest night, the slip, the spare-rope save, introduction not rescue. mana-r13 is [VP-Mana]'s record placement - almanac gets the hatch-day, rite record gets the method, the margin note gets neither - in her voice. mana-r14 carries [MT]/[S2-spine]/[S6-spine] the week's safe hatching and the red, blue, gold entries in the same tidy hand. mana-r15 carries [S7-spine]/[S3-spine]/[MT]/[MD-3] frost broken, crag named and protected, schedule in Claire's hand, the site that asked for hush getting a watch. mana-r16 carries [MT]/[MD-3] the flat spring, the patient bluebird, the true song returning after winter.

skillStages.planning: planning.md outputs restated for tier 5 and the shared-event format: the chapter is a beat script for ONE event with three tellings, not three adventures. The player's egg choice selects the telling at the front; the two-minute trip is a hard information gate; the telling's chronology and Neet's viewpoint live at or after trip-end. POV limits: pre-dispatch units carry S1-level facts, the chosen family's standing plight, and Neet's spoken intentions only - no decision made, no outcome, no legacies. Display order copied from the accepted premise (shared opening, then the route telling, then the traveler's viewpoint) and re-paced into boxes; because tier 5 has no hook/outcome pair, the plan sets an adaptation rule with a per-beat mapping layer instead of quote boxes. Each route got its growth: introductions for strangers (Life), learning to sing badly (Mana), reading and yielding to a wild mother's permission (Stamina). Route punishments: none; choices dispatch, then deliver.
skillStages.drafting: dialogue-and-behavior.md governs the boxes: the tellings stay prose in narrator beats with reported speech where the sources narrate lines; Neet's viewpoint facts become her voiced beats where her private record forms; the cast acts only per the selected telling, and Daisy's documented floor line is the single direct spoken line. Boxes target about 40 words; adapted confirm and final beats re-pace accepted sentences without changing facts. cognition-layers gates what the player can know before the trip ends.
skillStages.reviewing: revision-checklist pass per route: choice causality (option -> adapted confirm -> departure -> dispatch -> returns -> outcome), no pre-dispatch resolution scan, cast role-consistency per selected telling, spine coverage (S2-S7 per route) with route-owned outcomes never crossing routes, voice (Neet formal and dry in her own beats; narrator carries the tellings), material and job names byte-exact, box economy (43-token target), no player-award claims, and all three routes read back-to-back in source display order (Life, Mana, Stamina) for voice, cause and effect, repetition, and screen length.

characterNotes.neet: Formal, dry, ledger-minded; the shrine keeper of the five-keeper watch. Her tier-5 growth per route without needing earlier chapters: care that makes introductions until the crag reads strangers as tenants, while one honest grief stays in her margin and one feather is kept for the fledging day (Life); the correction habit reversed on purpose - learning to sing badly, and what that discipline costs at midnight, with the records sorted so the margin note gets neither (Mana); reading a wild mother's permission and answering it with one nod that is not in any record (Stamina). Portrait: 'neet' (established id, verified in source/core.js TRAVELERS: Neet_Portrait.png, file Neet_Portrait.webp in assets/characters/).
characterNotes.claire: The knight of the watch. Role stays inside the selected telling: Life - names the crag, files the protection, patrol schedule in her handwriting on the spot, and her log dates the frost's break; Mana - three nights of silence, the no-voices-past-the-tree-line rule, and the schedule once the quiet held; Stamina - cordons on the orchard path and every roofline, coming down into the schedule when they came down. Established traveler with an existing portrait (ClairePortrait.png, source/core.js TRAVELERS; file in assets/characters/). No spoken beat in this script: her work is narrator-carried (portrait 'none').
characterNotes.daisy: The baker of the watch. Life - the cold half of the problem (oven-warmed straw, heat only, quarter-twists like dough through its rise), one thick blanket answered with her documented floor line; Mana - warmed-straw restocks for the other ledges, the muffled quarter, warm bread so nobody must shout; Stamina - up all night, the first-light loaf that settles the move, and straw-lined carry baskets. Established traveler with an existing portrait (DaisyPortrait.png, source/core.js TRAVELERS; file in assets/characters/). Her one direct spoken line, life-r6, carries her portrait id 'daisy'.
characterNotes.dolbur: The warrior of the watch. Life - the first-evening rope drop that becomes an introduction; Mana - offers loudly to fight the frost, politely assigned elsewhere, frost-line rounds and the spare-rope save; Stamina - the winter climb, one bent piton reported immediately, and the one person the mother tolerates afterwards. Established traveler with an existing portrait (DolburPortrait.png, source/core.js TRAVELERS; file in assets/characters/). No spoken beat in this script: his work is narrator-carried (portrait 'none').
characterNotes.kyle: The challenger of the watch. Life - the one-handed catch, precisely named; Mana - cloth-wrapped rungs and hours of stillness [MT] (his count of seventeen silences and his pride in the hush holding without him stay with his own perspective chapter - owner revision pass removed them from mana-r9); Stamina - anchor and count of every carry, and the last coil into waiting hands. Established traveler with an existing portrait (KylePortrait.png, source/core.js TRAVELERS; file in assets/characters/). No spoken beat in this script: his work is narrator-carried (portrait 'none').

continuityFlags: Tier-5 deviation (documented): the pack's tier-5 entries are viewpoint texts with no hook/outcome pair, so this chapter has no byte-quote boxes; the confirm adapts the chosen family's plight and the final box adapts the route's lasting outcome, with the mapping layer citing each beat's source parts.

Shared-event discipline: one event, three tellings. Route-owned lasting outcomes (Life: the mixed roost and its trellis feathers; Mana: the hush custom and the working rite on record; Stamina: the quarry household on the map) never cross routes; spine facts S1-S7 are the only cross-route ground, per the pilot's recall rule.

The ensemble cast appears in every route per the selected telling's own roles; role-consistency is enforced per route and verified below. There is no foreign-name exclusion to run because the cast is shared by design; the scan instead checks that no route borrows another route's deeds or props.

No assumption the player has seen another family's route or an earlier Neet chapter: habits (ledger, margin, dry record voice) are shown fresh; no tier-1..4 callbacks; no route canon-locked, and later chapters may cite only spine facts and choice-independent growth.

Daisy's floor line is the only direct spoken line, quoted byte-exact from the accepted pilot; all other character actions are reported speech inside narration, matching the prose nature of the tellings. Other participants' private perspective material (Daisy's warm-center observation, Claire's private registers, Kyle's wind-check habit) belongs to their own future chapters and is not borrowed here.

Presentation notes from the accepted premise apply: the completed scene is stored for rereading in the replay journal and does not replay automatically on later visits; spacing and line-break handling of multi-line texts remains an HANDOFF open decision, untouched here.
